newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on India, Russia hopes.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on India, Russia hopes.

text.p: News India may be importing wheat rather than exporting and hopes for wheat business with Russia combined with short covering to boost CBOT wheat futures to a higher close, traders said.
"There is a lot of wheat business and it remains to be seen if the U.S. gets any of it," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

There was talk India was seeking 500,000 tonnes of wheat but there were signals Australia would be the likely supplier. Also an Indian newspaper said Wednesday the government was considering importing one million tonnes of wheat.
Traders said the potential business with Russia was being talked about but they remained skeptical about a significant sale of U.S. wheat to that region.
"They don't have any money and besides, that business would be later next year," a trader said.
Russian Agriculture Minister Viktor Khylstun said Russia would import up to three million tonnes of wheat in 1997.
Wheat also found support on talk Iraq may be a wheat buyer now that it has returned to the world oil market.
Wheat closed one to 5-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with December up 5-1/2 at $3.99.
In late dealings, there was news from Washington that helped confirm trade skepticism about sales of wheat to Russia.

"The former Soviet Union is no longer a factor in the world wheat market...it's not a player...they've got to have money to buy," said Gregg Doud of the U.S. Wheat Associates at a briefing in Washington on the world wheat outlook.

Key players in the wheat pit included Cargill Inc with 2.5 million bushels purchased in the July and Paine Webber bought 2.5 million March, traders said. Refco Inc bull spread 4.5 million bushels of March/July at 52-1/2 cents.
FIMAT Futures bought 2.5 million bushels of March and sold two million March, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, slightly below the 12,709 traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 1,100 March $4.00 calls at 9-3/4 cents and Smith Barney bought 900 March $4.30 calls at 3-3/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 2,000 contracts, above the 1,715 traded Tuesday.
